t: American statistician Herman Hollerith received a patent for his electromechanical tabulating machine for punched-card data.
Mirza Ghulam Ahmad founded the Ahmadiyya Islamic religious movement in British India.
The Treaty of Wuchale was signed, ending the Italo-Ethiopian War, but differences in translation later led to another war.
Bandits attacked a U.S. Army paymaster's escort in the Arizona Territory, stealing more than $28,000.
Bangui, the capital and largest city of the present-day Central African Republic, was founded in French Congo.
Hyde Park and several other Illinois townships voted to be annexed by Chicago, forming the largest city by area in the United States and the second-largest by population.
The New Zealand Native football team, predominantly comprising Māori players, concluded their 107-game tour, the longest in rugby union history.
Sir Henry Parkes, Premier of the Colony of New South Wales, gave a speech in which he called for the federation of the six Australian colonies.
Brazilian emperor Pedro II was overthrown in a coup led by Deodoro da Fonseca, while the country was proclaimed a republic.
